title: Hands-on Decision Sprint Agenda and Facilitator Cheatsheet
customer_focus: Early-stage Retail Analytics startup evaluating embed+chat integration for agentized search
required_materials: Miro board pre-populated with user journey and data schema
Test dataset sample (anonymized) shared via S3 link
Access to customer dev slack channel
prerequisites: Customer provides 1 sample dataset (CSV/json) and primary user persona
Customer agrees to account with hosted eval keys provisioned by SE
SE prepares minimal model variant list (quantized vs fp16) and latency estimates
Participants pre-read: 2-page one-pager on Redwood routing and fallback policies
objectives: Align on success criteria for the POC (SLA, throughput, acceptable latency and quality thresholds)
Run a lightweight hands-on experiment to validate model quality on 10 canonical prompts
Surface integration risks and decide on next-step deployment type (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
Capture concrete next steps and owners within the same day
agenda_timeline: 0:00–0:10 Welcome, goals, and roles (host + customer sponsor + engineers)
0:10–0:25 Customer context: data, UX flow, volume profile, and constraints
0:25–0:40 Quick architecture sketch: where Redwood sits, routing, telemetry hooks
0:40–1:10 Live demo: run 10 canonical prompts across 2 model variants and show latency/cost estimates
1:10–1:30 Breakout 1 (engineering): map integration points and identify data transformations
1:30–1:50 Regroup: present breakout findings and surface unknowns
1:50–2:20 Hands-on quality check: create and refine prompt templates, run batch evals
2:20–2:35 Breakout 2 (ops + security): discuss compliance, keys, VPC needs
2:35–2:50 Decision moment: recommended deployment option, acceptance criteria for POC
2:50–3:10 Roadmap planning: timeline, milestones, resource commitments
3:20–3:30 Wrap-up: owners, immediate next steps, follow-up meeting scheduling
slides_outline: Cover: workshop name, date, attendees, purpose
Customer snapshot: user personas, top 3 use cases, data characteristics
POC objective & success metrics (quality, latency, cost, security)
Candidate model variants and perf expectations
Integration touchpoints: call flow and telemetry
Breakout instructions and artifacts to produce
Decision checklist: infra, security, perf, cost
Appendix: eval scripts, endpoint configs, sample prompts
facilitator_cheatsheet: Before the session: confirm dataset is sanitized and accessible; provision temp eval keys
Kickoff: state the non-goal explicitly (e.g., not a full production readiness review)
Timebox rigorously; call out when to stop deep dives and move to decisions
During demos: show both success and failure cases to set realistic expectations
Encourage customer engineers to drive the keyboard in the hands-on segments
If discussion stalls on vendor procurement or contracts, park it and move to technical decision criteria
Use the Miro board to capture decisions live and assign owners inline
Close with an explicit acceptance criteria statement and sign-off plan
breakout_exercises: Engineering breakout (20 min): map 3 integration points and list required data transforms
Quality breakout (20 min): pick 5 target prompts, author test prompts and expected outputs
Ops/security breakout (15 min): list gating items for private deployment and estimated lift
Cost tradeoff quick-quiz (10 min): compute ballpark token cost for 1000 weekly active users
facilitation_roles_and_checklist: Lead facilitator: sets agenda, times sections, drives decision points
Demo engineer: runs live prompts, collects perf numbers, captures logs
Note taker: records decisions, owners, and open questions on action register
Customer sponsor: validates business success criteria and commits resources
Checklist: recording enabled, Miro ready, dataset access verified, eval keys provisioned
common_objections_and_suggested_response: Objection: "Latency looks higher than promised" — Response: show current SLOs and planned optimizations (quantization, routing), propose canary on dedicated pool
Objection: "We need on-prem for compliance" — Response: outline Redwood Private path and highlight audit/KMS integration effort estimate
Objection: "Costs unknown at scale" — Response: run a small scale projection using their volume profile and our batching/caching options and present unit economics
success_criteria: Average 95th percentile latency <= 600ms for 512-token requests in hosted baseline
Quality: human eval pass rate >= 85% on the 10 canonical prompts
Integration checklist completed: endpoints instrumented, error/backoff strategy defined
Customer signs off on POC acceptance criteria and agrees to timeline for next 4 weeks
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: data sensitivity blocks sharing sample data — Mitigation: use synthetic dataset and on-prem evaluation sandbox
Risk: customer infra QA window delays deployment — Mitigation: schedule staggered integration work and parallelize config work
Risk: model hallucination on domain-specific entities — Mitigation: create guardrail prompts and reranking step; include manual review for first 500 responses
follow_up_actions: SE to publish session recording and Miro board within 24 hours
Send formal POC proposal doc (timeline, scope, cost options) within 48 hours
Provision dedicated eval keys and small dedicated capacity run for 2 days (owner: Miguel Ortega)
Customer to provide anonymized expanded dataset and priority prompt list within 3 business days
Schedule technical kickoff for integration work within 5 business days
notes_to_self: Keep the session practical — prioritize surfaces that enable a binary decision (go/no-go) for POC type. Aim to leave with a signed scope rather than a vague interest.
file_notes: This is a lightweight workshop plan intended to be adapted per customer. If reused, change customer_focus, attached dataset links, and update success_criteria to match the customer's SLA needs.
